advisory.finding: The in-place refresh is bounded by `timeout 300`, but systemd kills the whole autodeploy oneshot after 90 seconds (`TimeoutStartSec=90`). A refresh that hangs or waits on a lock therefore kills the tick before `mcp_check_code_workspace` runs. The stuck-workspace page never fires, which is exactly the case it exists for. The rest of the no-op work (`mcp_retire_sweep`, `check_declared_compose_services`) is skipped too.
merged_from: `timeout` only terminates the host-side `docker exec` client. `docker exec` does not forward the signal, so the in-container refresh keeps running: its `git fetch`/`merge`, or its python lock waiter, which can wait up to `MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_WAIT=7200` s. Each later tick starts another refresh that queues on the same checkout lock, so orphaned refresh processes build up inside the live container while the tick reports only 'refresh failed'.

The refresh's stderr goes to `/dev/null`. That discards the entrypoint's refusal reason and its `MCP_CODE_WORKSPACE_ERROR {"reason": ...}` marker (dirty / unreachable / diverged), which the entrypoint emits so the host journal can count it. The freshness probe that follows cannot tell an unreachable remote from a diverged checkout (both read 'behind'), so the operator loses the actual cause.
scenarios: The remote (MCP_TICKETS_URL) stalls, so the in-container `git fetch` hangs. systemd SIGKILLs the tick at 90s every 2 minutes, `mcp-code-workspace-stuck` is never emitted, and gates silently read a stale tree.
A peer container's startup clone holds the code-checkout lock for minutes. Each tick blocks in `acquire_dir_lock` until systemd kills it, and the unit records repeated failures.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `timeout "$FETCH_TIMEOUT" docker exec -e MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_WAIT=5 "$name" sh /usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh --refresh-code`, i.e. a total budget that leaves room in the 90s unit timeout for the freshness check and the rest of the no-op tick.

advisory.finding: test_current_workspace_is_not_refreshed is a fail-open oracle. Its only behavioral check is that '--refresh-code' is absent from the docker command log. Nothing shows the HEAD probe exec ran, and `_commands` returns [] when the log file is missing. So the test also passes when the probe never ran, the stub's exec branch broke, or the log was never written.
scenarios: A regression makes the HEAD probe always fail or print nothing (for example a quoting break in MCP_CODE_HEAD_PROBE). Every behind workspace then silently skips refresh, yet this test stays green. Only the sibling test would catch it, and only as an indirect stuck-marker failure.
advisory.suggested_fix: Before the absence assertion, add `assert any(c.startswith("exec rebar-mcp-live-8092") for c in cmds), cmds`, then `assert _workspace_git(workspace, "rev-parse", "HEAD") == second` and `assert _stuck_markers(result) == []`.
